body: @michaelficarra, do you have any thoughts or insights here on how we might go about using escope on a JSX AST?  Is monkeypatching our best option, in your opinion?

The problem you're having is caused by esrecurse attempting to operate on unrecognised AST nodes by recursing onto every field in the object. In my opinion, esrecurse should fail immediately when it encounters an unrecognised AST node.

I don't like the monkeypatching of escope (I would prefer a specification be passed in instead), but it seems the best way to move forward given the current state of things.
@IanVS what version are you seeing this in? What is it you're trying to do?

I am seeing this in my [autoconfig branch](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/tree/autoconfig), which admittedly is slightly behind master.

I am trying to lint JSX code, get the `sourceCode`, and re-lint the `sourceCode`.

So it seems like the problem is the `parent` node confuses `esrecurse`?

Also seems like the right answer is for `esrecurse` to expose `Syntax` and `VisitorKeys` directly rather than relying on `estraverse`?

I think there are 3 approaches.
1. The right approach is that we send PRs to add an option for `visitorKeys` to `esrecurse` and `escope` (the `esrecurse` is used from `escope` internal). But it might take long time.
2. We make the `parent` property unenumerable: `Object.defineProperty(node, "parent", {value: parent, writable: true, configurable: true, enumerable: false})`. But I know this is very slow.
3. We use monkeypatching. It's quick and sloppy.

This PR is intended to provide an easy way to begin using ESLint on a non-linted project in a meaningful way. It will provide automatic creation of an ESLint configuration file based on the project files which will not result in linting errors when run against the project.

TODO:

- [x] Logic to repeatedly lint project files with sets of configurations to determine which rules can be enabled without erroring
- [x] Warning message for long execution
- [x] Extend `eslint:recommended`
- [x] Tests
- [x] Docs

Future Improvements:
- Autoconfigure React plugin rules
- Set rules to warn if only a few errors

We can try making `parent` nonenumerable, though we should doubke-check the perf impact (see https://www.nczonline.net/blog/2015/11/performance-implication-object-defineproperty/ )

I think ultimately making such changes to escope/esrecurse make the most sense.

I checked the performance change.
And I confirmed nonenumerable fixed this bug.

|  | Before | After | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| single file | 2422ms | 2515ms | +4% |
| multi files | 7480ms | 8294ms | +11% |

              */
             controller.traverse(ast, {
                 enter: function(node, parent) {
-                    node.parent = parent;
+                    Object.defineProperty(node, "parent", {
+                        value: parent,
+                        configurable: true,
+                        enumerable: false,
+                        writable: true
+                    });
                     eventGenerator.enterNode(node);
                 },
                 leave: function(node) {
